exposure: timing of prophylactic antibiotic administration (before skin incision)
timing of prophylactic antibiotic administration (after cord clamping)
cohort: The study included 356 pregnant females aged 20-45 years, at term, undergoing elective cesarean section for any indication.
finding: Prophylactic antibiotics administered 15-60 minutes before skin incision significantly reduced the rate of post-cesarean wound infection compared to administration after cord clamping (37.6% vs 62.4%, P<0.05).
